doc.title: Art Farmer — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: First piano lessons and copying his mother's hymns
summary: His musical start with a visiting white piano teacher at grammar school and with his mother's choir practice.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Like others, was this where you began your musical career, or was it in school?

Well actually, I began my musical career out of school because this was the time of the WPA, and everybody had a job. If you were a music teacher and you didn’t have a job, then they would give you a job teaching the kids. No, I’m jumping the gun. Actually, my music studying began in the grammar school where this white lady came by once a week and gave lessons on the piano, gave us an assignment to work on for the coming week. That was my first lesson.
Was that your choice to play piano?

Yeah, because we had a piano. Actually, my mother used to play for the choir before I started school, and I would go from the house to the church because we didn’t have the piano in the house at that time, we’d go to the church, and she would practice the hymns for the coming week. I would sit there with her, and after she got up from the piano, I would sit down and try to play them too.
